AVORIS_GENERAL.TITLE: Ávoris Travel
AVORIS_GENERAL.DESCRIPTION:
Ávoris is a <bold>travel group with 24 brands</bold>, such as <bold>B travel</bold>, <bold>Halcón Viajes</bold>, <bold>Iberojet</bold>, <bold>Marsol</bold>, <bold>Travelplan</bold> or <bold>Catai</bold>. It sells <bold>flights, hotels, transfers, car rental, tickets, tours and more</bold>, to two audiences: <bold>B2B</bold>, the travel agencies that sell its trips, and <bold>B2C</bold>, the customers who book directly. 

As a <bold>Product Designer</bold>, I work on the <bold>design of different projects</bold> of the group, for <bold>B2B and B2C</bold>, and on the <bold>Design System</bold> shared by all brands.

AVORIS_DS.TITLE: Ávoris Design System
AVORIS_DS.DESCRIPTION:
Ávoris has <bold>24 travel brands</bold>, and each product rebuilt the same components again and again. Design and code also drifted apart at every handoff. 

In a <bold>team of 3 designers</bold>, we built <bold>one design system for all brands</bold>: the same component works for 24 brands, and only the tokens change. <bold>AI turns each Figma component into code</bold> and checks it against the design. 

<bold>My part:</bold> I helped define how the variables are structured for 24 brands, and designed common components for B2B and B2C products. 

<bold>More than 500 components in code, 24 brands, one system.</bold>

AVORIS_FLIGHTS.TITLE: Ávoris Flights
AVORIS_FLIGHTS.DESCRIPTION:
A new case study about <bold>flights</bold>: the problem, how we solved it and what changed for the user. 

Built with the <bold>Ávoris Design System</bold>.

AYOBA_GENERAL.TITLE: Ayoba - South Africa
AYOBA_GENERAL.DESCRIPTION:
Ayoba is a <bold>SuperApp with 30 million</bold> monthly <bold>active users</bold> in more than <bold>15 African countries</bold> with 23 languages, including more than 8 African languages. <bold>MTN</bold> is the key investor, and one of the major telecommunications companies in Africa. 

Ayoba is a cross platform app (Android, iOS, PWA) and offers a range of services such as <bold>Chat, Voip, Music, Games, News, Microapps, Payments, Gifting and more.</bold> 

One of the key obstacles faced in Africa revolves around restrictes internet access, primarily attributed to high data costs and infrastructure challenges. 
Ayoba addresses this issue by providing complimentary data, aiming to foster digital inclusion and broaden access to digital communication for a larger population.

AYOBA_REDESIGN.TITLE: Redesign messaging for ayoba
AYOBA_REDESIGN.DESCRIPTION:
Ayoba is a <bold>SuperApp with 30 million</bold> monthly <bold>active users</bold> in more than <bold>15 African countries</bold> with 23 languages, including more than 8 African languages. <bold>MTN</bold> is the key investor, and one of the major telecommunications companies in Africa. 

Ayoba is a cross platform app (Android, iOS, PWA) and offers a range of services such as <bold>Chat, Voip, Music, Games, News, Microapps, Payments, Gifting and more.</bold> 

The <bold>central challenge revolved around identifying the key features in messaging</bold> that were crucial for redesign. Given that messaging constitutes the <bold>core feature in Ayoba</bold>, the objective was to enhance these features with the aim of boosting user retention and engagement.

AYOBA_USERPROFILE.TITLE: User Profile for ayoba
AYOBA_USERPROFILE.DESCRIPTION:
Ayoba is a super app, cross platform app (Android, iOS, PWA) and offers a range of services such as <bold>Chat, Voip, Music, Games, News, Microapps, Payments, Gifting and more.</bold> 

 <bold>Profile users</bold> are significant as it offers <bold>users the feeling that has a space</bold> and they are <bold>part of our ayoba community</bold>. To get our users the feeling of being part of our app we need to <bold>improve</bold> in areas such as <bold>discoverability, shared interest, customization, content sharing, discovering, privacy and security.</bold>

AYOBA_GAMES.TITLE: Games for ayoba
AYOBA_GAMES.DESCRIPTION: <bold>Ayoba want to provide a perfect integration of a new design with the existing app infrastructure</bold> while maintaining a <bold>consistent user experience across all features within the app.</bold> This involves coordinating with various teams (such as development, content, design, project managers, owners, QA and UX/UI) to update the games section without disrupting other functionalities like music, chat, and news.

AYOBA_MUSIC.TITLE: Music for ayoba
AYOBA_MUSIC.DESCRIPTION: While <bold>Ayoba has a strong user base for music</bold>, it lacks the diverse audio content that is so popular right now. The <bold>absence of podcasts on the platform limits Ayoba's ability to fully engage its audience</bold>, to stay relevant in the competitive landscape, Ayoba needs to implement a podcast feature within its music section.

NEWITTS_ECOMMERCE.TITLE: E-commerce for Newitts
NEWITTS_ECOMMERCE.DESCRIPTION: Newitts.com,  is one of the largest online sports wholesale r e-shops in the UK with a primary focus on catering to the UK market. The predominant segment of its e-commerce sales is centered around sports equipment and sportswear, serving Schools, Sports Clubs, Organizations, and administration. The e-store accounts for 70% of the total gross income.

OPTICA.TITLE: Try on Glasses
OPTICA.DESCRIPTION:
Try on glasses is an <bold>app for tablet</bold>, aimed at people who visit the physical stores of Optica Universitaria. 

Optica Universitaria stores face high customer traffic during peak times, leading to long wait times and dissatisfaction. The challenge was to enhance the in-store experience by <bold>providing a solution that allows customers to engage with products independently</bold> while waiting for sales assistance.

ABOUTME.TITLE: About
ABOUTME.DESCRIPTION:
Hello! I'm María, <bold>UX-UI designer with five years of experience</bold> in crafting engaging digital experiences for international projects. 

<bold>Currently based in Barcelona</bold>, my design journey has taken me across different countries, enriching my approach with diverse cultural perspectives. 

I have had the privilege of working with some of the <bold>world's leading companies, collaborating with global teams</bold> to deliver innovative solutions that meet user needs and business goals. <bold>My expertise is in understanding complex user journeys, creating intuitive interfaces, and ensuring seamless user interactions.</bold> 

I am passionate about every step of the design process—from research and ideation to prototyping and testing. Listening to users, uncovering their needs, and transforming insights into impactful designs is what drives me. 

I am dedicated to continuous learning and staying at the forefront of design trends and technologies. 

I am also highly skilled in <bold>teamwork, communication, and problem-solving. I do well in collaborative environments and thrive when working with diverse teams to achieve common goals. 

My adaptability and empathy allow me to connect with users and stakeholders effectively, ensuring that their needs are always at the forefront of my design solutions.</bold> 

In my portfolio, you'll find a selection of projects that showcase my ability to adapt to various challenges and deliver high-quality design solutions. Each project represents a unique story of collaboration, creativity, and problem-solving. I look forward to the opportunity to bring my experience and passion for design to new and exciting projects. Thank you for visiting my portfolio.

PROJECT_COMMON.FOOTER: If you would like to see more, don't hesitate to contact me!

OVERVIEW.TITLE: OVERVIEW
OVERVIEW.DESCRIPTION:
Ayoba is a <bold>SuperApp with 30 million</bold> monthly <bold>active users</bold> in more than <bold>15 African countries</bold> with 23 languages, including more than 8 African languages. <bold>MTN</bold> is the key investor, and one of the major telecommunications companies in Africa. 

Ayoba is a cross platform app (Android, iOS, PWA) and offers a range of services such as <bold>Chat, Voip, Music, Games, News, Microapps, Payments, Gifting and more.</bold> 

One of the key obstacles faced in Africa revolves around restricted internet access, primarily attributed to high data costs and infrastructure challenges. Ayoba addresses this issue by providing complimentary data, aiming to foster digital inclusion and broaden access to digital communication for a larger population.

CONTEXT.TITLE: Context of the problem
CONTEXT.DESCRIPTION:
Ayoba's primary emphasis lies in attracting new <bold>clients</bold> through comprehensive marketing strategies, <bold>user retention, and user registration on all platforms.</bold> 

<bold>The overarching goal is to elevate user engagement and maintain an active involvement on the platform.</bold> 

Acknowledging the pivotal role messaging plays in Ayoba's functionality, <bold>the company has strategically opted to enhance the messaging experience.</bold> This enhancement involves various facets, including improvements in technology, the visual design UI, new fueatures, user experience, and brand aesthetics.

PRIMARY_CHALLENGE.TITLE: Primary Challenge
PRIMARY_CHALLENGE.DESCRIPTION: The <bold>central challenge revolved around identifying the key features in messaging</bold> that were crucial for redesign. Given that messaging constitutes the <bold>core feature in Ayoba</bold>, the objective was to enhance these features with the aim of boosting user retention and engagement.

TEAM_COLLABORATION.TITLE: Team Collaboration
TEAM_COLLABORATION.DESCRIPTION: Messaging serves as the cornerstone feature in Ayoba, making it a substantial project. Another <bold>challenge was to collaborate closely with other teams, ensuring alignment and motivation across the board to collectively tackle this epic task.</bold>

ACCESSIBILITY.TITLE: Accessibility/Inclusivity
ACCESSIBILITY.DESCRIPTION: Embarking on a <bold>fresh UI design</bold>, the paramount objective is to maintain the essence of ayoba branding while <bold>prioritizing accessibility</bold>. The exploration involved a thoughtful <bold>selection of colors that not only align with ayobas brand identity but also contribute to creating an accessible product</bold>. Striking a balance between aesthetics and inclusivity is key, ensuring that the new UI is visually appealing while catering to users with diverse needs.

LEARNABILITY.TITLE: Learnability
LEARNABILITY.DESCRIPTION: In this phase of the project, the primary goal is to optimize learnability by <bold>crafting a product that is both familiar and easy to use</bold>. The design should facilitate a seamless learning curve for users, ensuring that interacting with the product feels intuitive and requires minimal effort to grasp.

PLATFORMS.TITLE: Platforms
PLATFORMS.DESCRIPTION: While developing the app, the main <bold>focus is based on Android users, giving them priority in terms of features and functionalities. However, post-project completion, there is a need to achieve parity for iOS and Progressive Web App (PWA) users.</bold>

AUDIT.TITLE: UX/UI Audit
AUDIT.DESCRIPTION: A comprehensive audit was conducted on the previous version to <bold>identify technical errors,  pain points, address accessibility issues, streamline user flows, and enhance visual design</bold>. This thorough examination aimed to identify and rectify any shortcomings or challenges present in the previous iteration, <bold>ensuring that the upcoming version delivers an improved and more seamless experience for users</bold>.

RESEARCH.TITLE: UX Research
RESEARCH.DESCRIPTION: <bold>Analyzing both quantitative and qualitative data</bold> was a critical aspect of the UX research process.  The quantitative data provided insights, offering a broad view of user <bold>behaviours and patterns</bold>. On the other hand, qualitative data, derived from interviews and surveys, provided a <bold>clear vision upon user experiences, preferences, and perceptions</bold>.

PRODUCT_PYRAMID.TITLE: Product Pyramid
PRODUCT_PYRAMID.DESCRIPTION: Creating a product pyramid for the messaging platform, was <bold>essential to structure features into three distinct levels</bold> that progressively address user needs and elevate the platform features. Each level builds upon the foundation laid by the previous one, providing a roadmap for the project's advancement.

WORKSHOP.TITLE: Workshops
WORKSHOP.DESCRIPTION: Conducting two workshop sessions with the entire ayoba team proved invaluable in uncovering both <bold>pain points and generating ideas for new features for the app</bold>. These collaborative sessions provided a platform for collective insights and brainstorming, fostering a shared vision among team members.

IDEATION.TITLE: Ideation and design work
IDEATION.DESCRIPTION: UX/UI exploration of <bold>new ideas and concepts</bold>.

PROTOTYPES.TITLE: Prototypes for Usability and A/B testing
PROTOTYPES.DESCRIPTION:
The primary goal was to gauge <bold>how effectively users could accomplish specific tasks</bold> within the new system and to <bold>pinpoint any pain points or challenges they encountered</bold>. 

A/B testing was employed to compare two or more versions of the design, aiming to identify which version performed better in terms of user engagement, conversion rates, or other relevant metrics.

FINAL_ITERATION.TITLE: Final Iteration
FINAL_ITERATION.DESCRIPTION: The final UX/UI iteration for the messaging platform was done by the incorporation of all new features and the valuable insights obtained from user tests.

SYSTEMS.TITLE: Design system
SYSTEMS.DESCRIPTION: <bold>The old design system was scaled up with new components</bold> and a new design system for iOS was created.

HANDOFF.TITLE: Handoffs
HANDOFF.DESCRIPTION: The delivery of high-fidelity deliverables marked a significant milestone, equipping developers and quality assurance (QA) teams with comprehensive resources for the implementation and testing phases. The deliverables included: User Stories, new UX/UI, interaction details, component specifications and usage guidelines.

QA.TITLE: QA and Demos
QA.DESCRIPTION: The UX/UI team provided support in demos for the QA process and final deliverables.

METRICS.TITLE: Metrics/KPIs
METRICS.DESCRIPTION: <bold>New events are created to track the results of the new UX/UI</bold>,  integrating analytics tools such firebase and google analytics.

AUDIT.TITLE: Audit
AUDIT.DESCRIPTION:
A comprehensive audit was conducted to <bold>identify pain points and areas for improvement in both the user interface (UI) and user experience (UX)</bold> 

The goal of this UX audit was to identify any potencial usability issues. 
Recommendations were based on

CRITICAL.TITLE: Critical- Tech, UX, UI
CRITICAL.DESCRIPTION: Critical violation: Urgent issues/bugs that <bold>disturb the user experience</bold>

AVERAGE.TITLE: Average- Tech, UX,UI
AVERAGE.DESCRIPTION: Average violation: Issues that can <bold>disturb some of the users and can improve the UX</bold>

LOW.TITLE: Low- Tech, UX, UI
LOW.DESCRIPTION: Low Violation: That might <bold>disturb a small percentage of users</bold>

KEY_INSIGHTS.TITLE: Key insights
KEY_INSIGHTS.DESC: We found that <bold>the app has significant issues in basic functionalities</bold>, fiixing these will greatly enhance  user satisfaction and usability.
KEY_INSIGHTS.DESC_2: Prioritize <bold>fixing critical bugs</bold> and enhancing key functionalities to <bold>improve immediate user experience</bold>.
KEY_INSIGHTS.DESC_3: <bold>Integrating more robust functionalities</bold> and enhancing media sharing capabilities (e.g., video editing, large file handling) can make the app more competitive and appealing to users.
KEY_INSIGHTS.DESC_4: The app's <bold>user interface requires significant updates</bold> to align with <bold>modern design principles, improve accessibility, and provide a consistent user experience</bold> across different devices.
KEY_INSIGHTS.DESC_5: Addressing issues like <bold>button visibility, contrast, and the clarity of interactive elements</bold> will improve accessibility.
KEY_INSIGHTS.DESC_6: Ayoba's unique offerings, such as <bold>free data for messaging</bold> and entertainment features, are strong selling points. <bold>Enhancing and promoting these features</bold> can differentiate Ayoba from competitors.
KEY_INSIGHTS.DESC_7: Improving the <bold>transparency of privacy settings</bold> and making them more accessible can reassure users about their data security.

SITE_MAP.TITLE: Site map
SITE_MAP.DESCRIPTION: The site map helped us to facilitates the <bold>evaluation of the messaging structure to identify potential vulnerabilitie or areas that could be exploited</bold>.

UX_RESEARCH.TITLE: UX research
UX_RESEARCH.DESCRIPTION:
<bold>Interviews and surveys</bold> were conducted by the UX researcher team, who played a pivotal role in gathering valuable insights.

The findings presented here offer merely a surface-level glimpse into the profound depth of this extensive investigation.

Me as a Owner of the project and with the support of the UX/UI team, I used this information to make <bold>important decisions, detected pain points, create new ideas features and improvements</bold>.

DEMOGRAPHICS.TITLE: Demographics
DEMOGRAPHICS.DESCRIPTION:
<bold>Africa</bold> has the world's <bold>youngest</bold> and <bold>fastest growing population</bold>.

<bold>Young people</bold> are generally more optimistic about the future, are more likely to believe that they can positively impact their country's governance, and are more likely to start their <bold>own busines</bold>.
DEMOGRAPHICS.DESCRIPTION_2: <bold>1.3 billion people already live in Africa - more people than in Europe and North America combined</bold>.

FEATURES.TITLE: Most features used in ayoba by Countries

BEHAVIOUR.TITLE: Browsing behaviour, technical competency
BEHAVIOUR.DESCRIPTION:
Our users all <bold>“Browse Facebook or Instagram or TikTok or Snapchat”</bold> 

In terms of <bold>messsaging platforms</bold> they use <bold>whatssap, messaging, instagram,telegram and moya</bold>.

MEDIA_BEHAVIOUR.TITLE: Text, image, video messaging behaviour
MEDIA_BEHAVIOUR.DESC: Users tend to send <bold>text messages to check in</bold> with their <bold>friends or family</bold>.
MEDIA_BEHAVIOUR.DESC_2: Sometimes they send  text messages if there is an urgency but is usually they use SMS for this scenario as they think it is faster and more trustworthy.
MEDIA_BEHAVIOUR.DESC_3: They feel more comfortable sending <bold>text messages in work enviroments</bold> than voice messages.
MEDIA_BEHAVIOUR.DESC_4: Regards to the messages of <bold>video an image</bold> they <bold>don't like the automatic download</bold> as they <bold>don't have a lot of space in their devices</bold>. They want to decide if they want to download these media

VOICE_MESSAGING.TITLE: Voice messaging behaviour
VOICE_MESSAGING.DESC: Some of our users have <bold>illiteracy Issues</bold>, so they use a lot the voice messages thats why it is an oportunity to have improvements in this area.
VOICE_MESSAGING.DESC_2: Other users are <bold>lazy to type</bold>, prefer voice messages.
VOICE_MESSAGING.DESC_3: Some users consider voice messages <bold>faster than typing</bold>
VOICE_MESSAGING.DESC_5: When they receive a voice messages <bold>they don't like others can hear it</bold>.

ACCESSIBILITY.TITLE: Accessibility
ACCESSIBILITY.DESCRIPTION:
<bold>Approximately 26.3 million</bold> people in the African Region are reported to have a form of <bold>visual impairment</bold>, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). 

<bold>Among them, 20.4 million individuals experience low vision</bold>, while an estimated <bold>5.9 million are considered blind</bold>.

OTHERS.TITLE: What users don't know about ayoba
OTHERS.SUBTITLE: Features
OTHERS.DESC_3: Doesn't know that one can create groups
OTHERS.DESC_4: Doesn't know that one can post stories

APPS.TITLE: Most popular apps in Africa
APPS.DESCRIPTION: Most popular apps in <bold>Africa</bold> are <bold>Whatsapp, Messenger, Telegram and other direct competitors are Moya and Sasai</bold>

INSIGHTS.TITLE: Insight & key-Findings
INSIGHTS.DESCRIPTION: The <bold>insights</bold> gained from the <bold>audit, site map, UX research, the benchmark and quantitative data from Firebase and Google Analytics</bold>, led to the following founds

PAIN_POINTS.TITLE: Pain points
PAIN_POINTS.DESC: Unfortunately, <bold>ayoba doesn't cover the bases of a platform messaging</bold>, it has a lot of <bold>wrong user flows, some basic features don't exist and also has features with technical problems</bold>.
PAIN_POINTS.DESC_2: As we saw in the research <bold>Africans</bold> have a lot of <bold>vision problems</bold> and Ayoba has to face significant accessibility challenges, primarily stemming from a <bold>low contrast between elements in the chat interface</bold>. Additionally, the font used is too light, <bold>compromising readability for users</bold>.
PAIN_POINTS.DESC_3: On our research, <bold>we identified literacy challenges</bold>, but <bold>Ayoba is not currently prioritizing accessibility</bold> measures for these users.
PAIN_POINTS.DESC_4: Still some <bold>inconsistency throughout the app UI, iconography, buttons, etc</bold> (can make the user feel confused)
PAIN_POINTS.DESC_6: <bold>Contacts do not sincronyze correctly with native device</bold>.
PAIN_POINTS.DESC_7: Some <bold>features don't work correctly between platforms Androdi-iOS and PWA</bold>.
PAIN_POINTS.DESC_8: Some basic <bold>features</bold> are very <bold>difficult for our users to find them</bold>, (create a group, invite friends, archive chat etc). (Bad AI)
PAIN_POINTS.DESC_9: There is a <bold>high percentage of churn because users feel don't have enough contacts on ayoba</bold>.
PAIN_POINTS.DESC_10: Users <bold>would love to invite their friends and family to use ayoba but they don't know how to do it</bold>.
PAIN_POINTS.DESC_11: <bold>Ayoba is very far away from its competitors</bold> in terms of good user experience and offers nice features in messaging .

INSIGHTS.TITLE: Insights
INSIGHTS.DESC: Despite all the problems we found in Ayoba messaging, users use the app because <bold>most of the features in ayoba come with Free Data</bold>.
INSIGHTS.DESC_2: <bold>Free data is the big value</bold> of ayoba against our competitors .
INSIGHTS.DESC_3: Even though our users complain that they would like to have more contacts, <bold>messaging is the most used feature in ayoba</bold>.
INSIGHTS.DESC_4: Users would like to express themselves on chat with new features as reactions.
INSIGHTS.DESC_5: Users would like to be able to <bold>browse the app while they have voice calls on</bold>.
INSIGHTS.DESC_6: For users is important to <bold>have social features on messaging</bold>.

SOLUTIONS.TITLE: Solutions
SOLUTIONS.DESC: Based on the research, audit and benchmark the <bold>priority is to cover the core of a messaging platform with a good experience</bold>.
SOLUTIONS.DESC_2: <bold>Accessibility for people with vision problems is a must</bold>, ayoba has to work in better contrast and better readability. (WCAG)
SOLUTIONS.DESC_3: <bold>For users who may face challenges with reading and writing ayoba has to improve on the feature of voice notes</bold> as come up with <bold>new solutions as subtitles, voice command etc</bold> ( 3rd level feature)
SOLUTIONS.DESC_4: Improve layouts for better readability and an intuitive navigation.
SOLUTIONS.DESC_5: Address the clutter on the messaging feature having <bold>consistency in the UI.</bold>
SOLUTIONS.DESC_6: Relocate options that users are looking for and cannot find with a <bold>better information architecture (Invite friends)</bold>
SOLUTIONS.DESC_7: Once the bases cover the team can start working to land the ideas for high features which means specific features for our users.

PRODUCT_PYRAMID.TITLE: Product Pyramid
PRODUCT_PYRAMID.DESCRIPTION:
The <bold>product strategy pyramid</bold> was established to visualize the product build strategy.

The strategy is divided into three levels, each addressing specific aspects and progressively advancing the project to where we want to go. <bold>Defining the foundation/basis</bold> covers the basics of the messaging app and <bold>when moving up the pyramid</bold> we address high and specific features for our users.

WORKSHOP.TITLE: Workshop
WORKSHOP.DESCRIPTION:
Conducting two workshop sessions with the entire Ayoba team proved invaluable in uncovering both pain points and generating ideas for new features for the app. 
These collaborative sessions provided a platform for collective insights and brainstorming, fostering a shared vision among team members.

NEW_DESIGN.DISCLAIMER: ***Be aware that you are only seeing 5% of all the work that was done.

FEED_CHAT.TITLE: Feed Chat
FEED_CHAT.DESC: Definition of contact cards with different elements

P2P_CHAT.TITLE: P2P Chat
P2P_CHAT.DESC: Definition of Message Speech Bubble. (Open, Middle, Close).
P2P_CHAT.DESC_2: Definition of spacings between (sender and receiver) bubbles.
P2P_CHAT.DESC_4: Definition of spacings between same P2P bubbles.
P2P_CHAT.DESC_9: The contrast between bubble background and text, passed the contrast checker from WCAG 3.0 guidelines.

CONTEXT.TITLE: Context of the problem
CONTEXT.DESCRIPTION:
The main functionality in ayoba is <bold>messaging and our goal is to improve different functionalities in this field</bold>.

We notice that <bold>profile users</bold> are significant as it offers our <bold>users the feeling that has a space</bold> and they are <bold>part of our ayoba community</bold>. To get our users the feeling of being part of our app we need to <bold>improve</bold> in areas such as <bold>discoverability, shared interest, customization, content sharing, discovering, privacy and security</bold>.

BENCHMARK.TITLE: Benchmark
BENCHMARK.DESCRIPTION:
A benchmark of our competitors helps us to detect <bold>what we are doing badly in this feature</bold> and allow us to discover <bold>patterns in user profiles that follow different apps</bold> such as architecture information, ways of edition information, shortcuts etc 

<bold>This Benchmark aimed to identify and rectify pain points present in the current design</bold>.

PERSONALIZATION.TITLE: Personalization and customization
PERSONALIZATION.DESC:
We found that personalization or customization appear in various apps that we studied. Depending on the app's focus, the priority is to highlight the personalization or customization.
<bold>Social networking apps like Facebook and Telegram have more customization in their user profiles, while apps like WhatsApp and Gojek may focus more on personalisation (basic info of their users)</bold>.

PRIVACY.TITLE: Privacy Considerations
PRIVACY.DESC:
<bold>All platforms place importance on user privacy</bold> and provide different levels of control over profile visibility. 
Privacy controls are <bold>essential for maintaining user trust</bold> and ensuring a positive user experience.

DISCOVERABILITY.TITLE: Discoverability and Engagement:
DISCOVERABILITY.DESC:
<bold>Facebook and Telegram prioritize the discoverability</bold> of user profiles to encourage connections and community engagement within their platforms. <bold>While WhatsApp has a stronger emphasis on privacy</bold> and direct communication, resulting in less discoverability of user profiles.

On the other side, we can find a lot of design patterns such as profile picture thumbnails, profile picture cropping, privacy settings (visibility for pictures and number phone) and good resolution and quality of the image.

OBJECTIVES.TITLE: Define Objectives
OBJECTIVES.DESCRIPTION:
The <bold>intention</bold> behind this <bold>research is to view the profile and settings of business requirements holistically</bold> and to tap into each stakeholder's knowledge and vision so that business requirements are aligned.
As is important to also detect pain points through usability testing on the current profile with ayoba users
This foundation will be built upon and prototypes or designs will be shown to users to see whether we align with their needs

CURRENT_PROFILE.TITLE: What ayoba users think about current profile
CURRENT_PROFILE.DESCRIPTION:
<bold>Limited Customization:</bold>
"I wish there were more options to customise my profile, like adding a status message or a bio"

<bold>Profile Picture Issues:</bold>
"The profile picture has very bad quality when you upload it"

<bold>Navigation Difficulties:</bold>
"Finding certain profile settings can be confusing; they're not very intuitive"

<bold>Edition Difficulties:</bold>
"It's very complex to understand how I can change my nickname or add more personal information, also to update my image"

<bold>Privacy Concers:</bold>
"I'm not sure how my information is used and who can see my profile details"

<bold>Lack of Social Features:</bold>
"It would be nice if the profile section included social media links such as Facebook, Instagram, etc"

INSIGHTS.TITLE: Insights & key-Findings
INSIGHTS.DESCRIPTION: The <bold>insights</bold> gained from the <bold>audit, site map, UX research, the benchmark and quantitative data from Firebase and Google Analytics</bold>, led to the following founds:

PAIN_POINTS.TITLE: Pain points
PAIN_POINTS.DESC: The user profile screen doesn't cover some basic features; unfortunately, the features that Ayoba has suffer from poor usability and accessibility.
PAIN_POINTS.DESC_2: Inconsistency throughout the app UI, iconography, buttons, etc
PAIN_POINTS.DESC_3: Few options in the user profile, which makes it difficult to users feeling is their space to show themselves to the ayoba world.
PAIN_POINTS.DESC_5: Inconsistency design between platforms AND & IOS.
PAIN_POINTS.DESC_6: Ayoba is very far away from its competitors in terms of good user experience and offers nice features such personalization, customization and privacy considerations for the user profile.

INSIGHTS.TITLE: Insights
INSIGHTS.DESC: Users would like a space to show themselves and see others, just not with a picture profile, they want to show their favourite games, music history, stories, etc
INSIGHTS.DESC_2: Users would like to express themselves.
INSIGHTS.DESC_3: Users would like to know what have in common with others users such as chat groups or entertainment interests.
INSIGHTS.DESC_4: After some interviews using the current design, users would like to have a space where they can share their social media as Instagram, Facebook, etc

SOLUTIONS.TITLE: Solutions
SOLUTIONS.DESC: Based on the research, audit and benchmark the priority is to cover the bases of a user profile.
SOLUTIONS.DESC_2: Fix accessibility and consistency is mandatory.
SOLUTIONS.DESC_4: Improve layouts for better readability and an intuitive navigation.
SOLUTIONS.DESC_5: Improve the architecture of information in order to have clarity with the different sections on user profile.
SOLUTIONS.DESC_6: Once the bases cover the team can start working to land the ideas for high features which means specific features for our users.

CONTEXT.TITLE: Context of the problem
CONTEXT.DESCRIPTION:
One of the <bold>most important things for Ayoba is offering its users the best entertainment with free data</bold> to provide the population with digital inclusion. (Many parts of Africa have limited access to the internet due to high data costs and limited infrastructure.)

<bold>Free data allows users to access essential digital services such as communication and entertainment.</bold>

Ayoba is always looking to offer its users the best content within the app. Therefore, <bold>Ayoba wanted to update the content games and would add more than 64 new games to its games section.</bold> However, <bold>the overall monthly report showed us that games were in a disadvantageous position compared to other features such as music, chat, and news.</bold> Considering that we were going to include new modern games, and in the long term maybe to have paid games business decided to give more care to this section and do a complete redesign aligned with other sections within the app.

<bold>The main goal of this project is to enhance and redesign the games section within the Ayoba app to improve its user experience and alignment with other app features, in preparation for the inclusion of new modern games and the potential introduction of paid games in the future.</bold>

PRIMARY.TITLE: Primary Challenge
PRIMARY.DESCRIPTION: The central challenge to redesigning the games section in the Ayoba app was to <bold>provide a perfect integration of the new design with the existing app infrastructure</bold> while maintaining a <bold>consistent user experience across all features within the app.</bold> This involves coordinating with various teams (such as development, content, design, project managers, owners, QA and UX/UI) to update the games section without disrupting other functionalities like music, chat, and news.

TEAM.TITLE: Team Collaboration
TEAM.DESCRIPTION: Another challenge was to collaborate closely with other teams, <bold>this involves coordinating with various teams (such as development, content, design, project managers, owners, QA and UX/UI)</bold> to update the games section without disrupting other functionalities like music, chat, and news.

PLATFORMS.TITLE: Platforms
PLATFORMS.DESCRIPTION: While developing the app, the main focus is based on <bold>Android and iOS</bold> users, giving them priority in terms of features and functionalities. However, post-project completion, there is a need to achieve parity for Progressive Web App (PWA) users.

AUDIT.TITLE: UX-UI Audit
AUDIT.DESCRIPTION: An <bold>audit was conducted with the previous version</bold> of the redesign of games to identify <bold>critical, average and low issues</bold> regards the UX/UI. with the goal of identifying and rectifying any problems found, offering our users the best user experience.

INSIGHTS.TITLE: Key insights
INSIGHTS.DESCRIPTION: We found that the section games have the following issues:

HIERARCHY.TITLE: Visual Hierarchy
HIERARCHY.DESC: The <bold>old layout lacks a clear visual hierarchy</bold>. All <bold>content</bold> is at the <bold>same level</bold>, which means there is no important content or content that we can suggest to the user to open to have an engagement with the games section.

APPEAL.TITLE: Visual Appeal
APPEAL.DESC:
The design is <bold>too simple and might not be visually appealing</bold> to all users. It might benefit from more engaging pics of games or a more dynamic and modern layout.

The screen <bold>does not provide detailed information</bold> about individual games up front. Users need to navigate further to get details about specific games.

NAVIGATION.TITLE: Navigation
NAVIGATION.DESC:
The navigation <bold>doesn't allow the user at first sight to get encouraged to play a game</bold>, the user is <bold>not provided detailed information</bold> about individual games up front or next-screen permissions. Users need to navigate further to get details about specific games.
<bold>There is no place to find the games I played and my favourites.</bold>
And more seriously the <bold>user can not start playing straight forward the game</bold> from the main screen of the games.

ACCESSIBILITY.TITLE: Accessibility
ACCESSIBILITY.DESC: The <bold>old design's red background might be too attention-grabbing, and distracting</bold>, and could overwhelm the user and give a sensation of clutter.

PERMISSION.TITLE: Content Permission
PERMISSION.DESC: The screen <bold>provides unclear information</bold> about the permissions required by the game, <bold>which is essential for user trust and transparency.</bold>

UX_RESEARCH.TITLE: UX research
UX_RESEARCH.DESCRIPTION:
<bold>Through data from Firebase</bold>, we realized how many users use the game section. with this data, we realized users use it very little compared with messaging, music etc. The results were scary as <bold>only 7% of our active users used games</bold>. In interviews with users we found:

<bold>Content</bold>
Users <bold>expressed dissatisfaction with the game content</bold>, describing it as <bold>"old" and "boring"</bold> fortunately the part of ayoba business was working on <bold>diversifying the game offerings by adding new, engaging games</bold>. And <bold>having in mind regularly update the game library</bold> to keep users interested.

<bold>Look& feel</bold>
Referring to the appearance users mentioned that games "feel super old" and that they "don't understand the illustrations"

<bold>Updating the game UI</bold>
Modernize the design, improve graphics, and ensure a consistent visual style.

<bold>User Engagement</bold>
Having the data from <bold>Firebase and metrics</bold> such;
How many times user open games per day?, How long do users spend playing games?, Do they complete levels or abandon them quickly?, Are there specific game types that perform better?. <bold>We had the result that the low usage rate is only 7% of active users. It indicates an urgent need for improvement.</bold>

CONTEXT.TITLE: Context of the problem
CONTEXT.DESCRIPTION:
Ayoba has recognized the growing demand for diverse audio content. To stay competitive and satisfy its users, Ayoba is exploring ways to expand its content offering podcasts.

<bold>The addition of podcasts to the music section is seen as a strategic move to increase engagement and enhance the platform.</bold>

While <bold>Ayoba has a strong user base for music</bold>, it lacks the diverse audio content that is so popular right now. The <bold>absence of podcasts on the platform limits Ayoba's ability to fully engage its audience</bold>, to stay relevant in the competitive landscape, Ayoba needs to implement a podcast feature within its music section.

<bold>This new feature allows users to access high-quality, multiple content new experiences within the app</bold>, increasing their satisfaction, retention, and overall platform usage.

PRIMARY.TITLE: Primary Challenge
PRIMARY.DESCRIPTION: The <bold>primary objective is to discover how to integrate podcasts into Ayoba's music</bold> section and <bold>guarantee a seamless and intuitive user experience</bold> while also improving and updating the UI.

TEAM.TITLE: Team Collaboration
TEAM.DESCRIPTION: Working <bold>very closely with the UX researcher</bold> expert was crucial as the design team and business didn't know if our users were ready for this podcast implementation.

ACCESSIBILITY.TITLE: Accessibility
ACCESSIBILITY.DESCRIPTION: As Ayoba aimed to introduce the podcast feature to the music section, the team saw an <bold>opportunity to address several accessibility issues.</bold> One key area of focus was <bold>improving the contrast colors of the miniplayer</bold>, which appears across various sections such as messaging, games, news, and more. This enhancement ensures a consistent and accessible user experience throughout the entire platform.

PLATFORMS.TITLE: Platforms
PLATFORMS.DESCRIPTION: The main focus is based on <bold>Android</bold> users.

CONTENT.TITLE: Content
CONTENT.DESC: <bold>Most of the apps</bold> studied <bold>provide a diverse and extensive library of podcasts</bold> covering various genres and interests.

PERSONALIZATION.TITLE: Personalization
PERSONALIZATION.DESC: Other apps <bold>offers personalized podcast recommendations</bold> based on listening habits.

COLLECTIONS.TITLE: Curated Collections
COLLECTIONS.DESC: Features curated lists and collections of popular podcasts.

UI.TITLE: User Interface
UI.DESC: <bold>Design a clean, intuitive interface</bold> that is <bold>easy to navigate</bold> and visually appealing.

MONETIZATION.TITLE: Monetization
MONETIZATION.DESC: <bold>Explore multiple monetization strategies including ads, sponsored content</bold>, and subscription models for premium content.

OFFLINE.TITLE: Download and Offline Listening
OFFLINE.DESC: Almost all platforms supports downloading episodes for offline playback.

UX_RESEARCH.TITLE: UX research
UX_RESEARCH.DESCRIPTION:
To successfully implement a podcast feature in Ayoba's music section, it's essential to conduct comprehensive UX research. This will help understand user needs, preferences, and pain points.

<bold>Its important to define research objectives, in this case for this project we will need to identify if our users are ready to understand what is a podcast, what kind of content they are interested</bold> etc. as <bold>studying our competitors, look for patterns</bold> they share, <bold>understand strengths and weaknesses of competitors' podcast</bold> features.

DEMOGRAPHICS.TITLE: Demographics
DEMOGRAPHICS.DESC_1: The survey was primarily conducted in <bold>English-speaking countries, with Nigeria, Uganda, South Africa, and Ghana accounting for 84% of the responses.
DEMOGRAPHICS.DESC_2: <bold>The dominant age groups were 25-34, followed by 18-24 and 35-44. The majority of respondents were male and either still in school or had a high school diploma.

AWARENESS.TITLE: Podcast Awareness and Preferences
AWARENESS.DESC_1: <bold>56% of participants understood the term "podcast",</bold> and of those, only 14% did not listen to podcasts at all.
AWARENESS.DESC_2: There is a <bold>preference</bold> for a <bold>mix of local and international podcasts</bold>, with a slight bias towards local content.
AWARENESS.DESC_3: Those with <bold>higher education levels</bold> are more <bold>inclined to listen to podcasts</bold>, suggesting that educating users could increase engagement.

CONTENT.TITLE: Content and Topics
CONTENT.DESC_1: <bold>Users favour</bold> podcasts that focus on <bold> local topics, particularly those concerning government and organizations.</bold>
CONTENT.DESC_2: There is a <bold>significant interest in categorizing podcasts based on geographical context</bold>, with clear distinctions between local and international content.

LOCAL_CONTENT.TITLE: Local Content
LOCAL_CONTENT.DESC_1: 12% of respondents mentioned that they could not relate to international podcasts, and 8% cited language barriers as a reason for not listening to podcasts.
LOCAL_CONTENT.DESC_2: <bold>There is a clear demand for hyperlocal podcasts</bold> that resonate with the local audience's experiences and language preferences.

PODCAST_TOPICS.TITLE: What topics should be focused on in podcasts?

WHY_PODCASTS.TITLE: Why do people listen to podcast?
WHY_PODCASTS.DESCRIPTION: The successful integration of podcasts into Ayoba's music section will require a strategic approach focusing on user education, content localization, and seamless user experience. Ayoba can enhance its value proposition and significantly increase user engagement with the music vertical.

OVERVIEW.TITLE: OVERVIEW
OVERVIEW.DESCRIPTION: Newitts.com, is <bold>one of the largest online sports wholesaler</bold> e-shops in the UK with a <bold>primary focus on catering to the UK market</bold>. The predominant segment of its e-commerce sales is <bold>centered around sports equipment and sportswear, serving Schools, Sports Clubs, Organizations, and administration. The e-store accounts for 70% of the total gross income.</bold>

MOBILE_FIRST.TITLE: Mobile-First Approach
MOBILE_FIRST.DESCRIPTION: Our design approach prioritizes a mobile-first strategy, ensuring a seamless and user-friendly experience on smartphones and tablets. The interface will be responsive, optimizing content for various screen sizes and resolutions.

NAVIGATION.TITLE: Main Navigation
NAVIGATION.DESCRIPTION: Simplify the main navigation to enchance user experience. Implement a clean and intuitive menu structure with easily recognizable symbols and concise labels. Streamline categories for easy access to products, ensuring a hassle-free browsing experience.

ARCHITECTURE.TITLE: Information Architecture
ARCHITECTURE.DESCRIPTION: Revise the information architecture to provide a logical and intuitive flow, Group related products and categories, making it effortless for users to find what they need, suggest a search bar with auto-suggestions to expedite the navigation process.

CHECKOUT.TITLE: Streamlined Checkout Process
CHECKOUT.DESCRIPTION: Optimize the checkout process for efficiency and user satisfaction. Implement a multi-step checkout with progress indicators to keep users informed about their current stage. Include guest checkout options for a seamless transaction experience.

BRANDING.TITLE: Branding Enhancement
BRANDING.DESCRIPTION: Refine the branding elements to create a cohesive and memorable visual identifiy. Utilize a modern color palette, new typography, and high-quality imagery that aligns with the brand image.

UX.TITLE: General UX Improvements
UX.DESCRIPTION: Address general UX issues by enchancing page loading speed, minimizing pop-ups, and ensuring a clutter-free design. Prioritize readability with clear font choices and appropriate text sizes. Implement user feedback where necessary to continually refine the user experience.

UI.TITLE: Modern and Clutter-Free UI
UI.DESCRIPTION: Create a modern and visually appealing UI that focuses on showcasing products and categories. Utilize high-resolution images, prominent call-to-action buttons, and subtle animations to engage users. Prioritize a minimalist design to reduce visual clutter and ailing with industry and target standards.

PRIMARY.DESCRIPTION:
<bold>The primary challenge</bold> of this project is to collaborate effectively with the tech team and accomodate the existing CMS capabilities and limitations. The initial stage involves the development of a (MVP) with minimal backend modifications. The key objectives include improving site navigation and Information Architecture (IA) without altering the current backend architecture. The proposed solutions aims to address existing frontend issues while laying the foundation for a scalable structure that accommodates future functionalities and features.

• <bold>Scalability:</bold> Develop a scalable solution that allows for easy integration of new functionalities and features in the future.

SECONDARY.DESCRIPTION:
The challenge for the visual design and re-branding, this strategy aims to strike a balance between industry standards, brand consistency, and practical considerations, fostering a visually appealing and trustworthy online presence within the initial budget for this MVP. A new Brand typography was also selected.

AUDIT.DESCRIPTION: This thorough exercise aimed to provide valuable insights, address existing issues, and explore opportunities for innovation.
AUDIT.ANALYSIS: <bold>Page-by-Page Analysis:</bold> A detailed examination of each main page, including the homepage, product pages, categories pages, and checkout process, was conducted to identify specific pain points.
AUDIT.JOURNEY: <bold>User Journey Assessment:</bold> The audit focused on evaluating the user journey, from landing on the site to completing a purchase. This involved analyzing navigation, page load times, and overall user flow.
AUDIT.COMPATIBILITY: <bold>Cross-Device Compatibility:</bold> The audit considered the website's performance and usability across various devices, ensuring a seamless experience for users on desktops, tablets, and mobile devices.

INSIGHTS.TITLE: Insights
INSIGHTS.SUBTITLE: The insights gained from the website audit, validated by client discussions and cross-referenced with quantitative data from Google Analytics, led to the following key recommendations:

HOMEPAGE.TITLE: Homepage
HOMEPAGE.DESC_1: Focus on a versatile Homepage Information Architecture (IA) that aims to introduce a dynamic and modular structure that aligns with seasonal campaigns, new marketing initiatives, product launches, brand promotions, and special offers. The goal is to create a scalable IA that adapts to evolving product requirements and allows for diverse tracking events to enchance conversion rates.
HOMEPAGE.DESC_2: Address the clutter on the homepage, proposing a cleaner design that prioritizes key product categories and highlights special offers.
HOMEPAGE.DESC_3: Implement SEO-generated content blocks to enchance organiz search placement.
HOMEPAGE.DESC_4: The enhanced Homepage IA, should embrace versatility and modularity, to deliver a dynamic and engaging experience for users while providing the flexibility needed to adapt to evolving marketing and product requirements.

The extensive list of anchors has proven to be cumbersome, leading to low user engagement based on both testing results (Analytics) and stakeholder feedback.
CATEGORY.DESC_4: Prioritize a mobile-first approach to ensure a seamless and user-friendly experience on smaller screens.
CATEGORY.DESC_5: Address the low user engagement observed on these pages by creating a more compelling and user-centric layout.

CHECKOUT.TITLE: Checkout Process

INTRO.DESCRIPTION:
<bold>A design system for many brands, connected to code with AI</bold>.

As part of the 3-person team that designed Ávoris' new design system from scratch, I helped define <bold>how variables are structured so one component works for 24 brands</bold>, and designed <bold>common components used across every B2B and B2C project</bold>.

<bold>8 Figma files · 24 brands · B2B and B2C</bold> · flights, hotels, transfers, cars, tickets, tours…

CONTEXT.TITLE: The context
CONTEXT.DESCRIPTION: Ávoris is a travel group with many brands. The system had to work for three things at the same time:
CONTEXT.BRANDS: <bold>24 brands.</bold> Each brand has its own colors, shapes and logo: <bold>B travel</bold>, <bold>Halcón Viajes</bold>, <bold>Marsol</bold>, <bold>Iberojet</bold>, <bold>Muchoviaje</bold>, <bold>Travelplan</bold>, <bold>Welcome</bold>, <bold>Catai</bold>…
CONTEXT.LINES: <bold>Many lines of business:</bold> <bold>flights, hotels, transfers, car rental, tickets, tours and more.</bold> Each line needs its own special components.
CONTEXT.AUDIENCES: <bold>Two audiences:</bold> <bold>B2B</bold>, the travel agencies that sell our trips, and <bold>B2C</bold>, the customers who book directly with us.
CONTEXT.LOGIC: All these combinations follow the same product logic: <bold>search, compare, book and pay.</bold> Without a shared system, each project built the same components again and again.
CONTEXT.HOMES: You can already see this idea on the group's websites. The homes of <bold>B travel</bold> and <bold>Halcón Viajes</bold> are not part of this Design System, but they follow the same concept: <bold>the same structure and the same components, each with its own brand.</bold>
CONTEXT.HOVER: Hover to see the whole page

PROBLEM.TITLE: The problem
PROBLEM.SUBTITLE: Too many brands, too many repeated components, and little time to launch new projects.
PROBLEM.P_1: With <bold>24 brands and many projects</bold>, the same component was built many times, in Figma and in code, in versions that were almost the same. <bold>Every change had to be repeated in all of them.</bold>
PROBLEM.P_2: <bold>A brand didn't always look the same.</bold> The same button of one brand could look different in flights and in tickets, so the brand felt less consistent for the user.
PROBLEM.P_3: <bold>Design and code drifted apart:</bold> every handoff to development could add small differences.
PROBLEM.P_4: <bold>The business needs to move fast.</bold> When it asks for a new project, we can't start from zero, but some businesses also need to stand out from the rest.
PROBLEM.NEEDED_DESC: <bold>A design system organized by lines of business</bold>, with shared components at its base (CORE, common for B2B or B2C, and specific per project). This gives us:
PROBLEM.NEEDED_1: <bold>Reuse.</bold> Each component is built once and used across projects and brands. A change is made in one place.
PROBLEM.NEEDED_2: <bold>Consistency.</bold> Every project uses the same component with the brand's tokens, so a brand looks the same in flights, tickets or hotels.
PROBLEM.NEEDED_3: <bold>Speed.</bold> New projects start from the common components that already exist for their line.
PROBLEM.NEEDED_4: <bold>Customization when needed.</bold> A business that needs to stand out gets its own variants of the shared components, instead of new ones.
PROBLEM.NEEDED_5: <bold>Easy to document.</bold> Each component lives in its level, so we always know if it is a common element or which project it belongs to. This makes every component easier to document, find and maintain.
PROBLEM.NEEDED_CODE: <bold>Connected to code.</bold> Each component built in code from Figma, with the same names, and checked against the design, so design and code stop drifting apart. <bold>This is where AI comes in.</bold>
PROBLEM.LIMITATION: <bold>The limitation:</bold> we don't have access to the front-end repository yet, so for now the code lives in our own repository.

EVOLUTION.TITLE: The journey
EVOLUTION.DESCRIPTION: We started this design system <bold>two years ago</bold>, when AI was not yet ready to work with Figma and code. So we first built everything <bold>by hand in Figma</bold>. As AI improved, we added it to our process to <bold>take the design to code</bold>. This is the journey, in three steps:

STEP_ONE.TITLE: Step 1. Where we started: one system in Figma
STEP_ONE.DESCRIPTION: First, we put order in Figma: we decided <bold>where each component lives</bold> and how <bold>one component can work for 24 brands</bold>. This order is what later made it possible to take the system to code with AI.

STRUCTURE.TITLE: Three levels of scope
STRUCTURE.DESCRIPTION: We organized the system into <bold>8 Figma files</bold>, based on <bold>where each component is used</bold>: CORE for every project, common components for all the projects of B2B or of B2C, and specific components for one project only. Three more files hold the base: Icons, Logos and Variables.

SLOTS.TITLE: Slots: one component, many uses
SLOTS.P_1: A <bold>slot</bold> is an empty space inside a component where you can put other content. It's like a picture frame: the frame doesn't change, but you can put any photo inside.
SLOTS.P_2: For example, our transfer card has spaces for the image, the tags, the price and the button. <bold>The card decides where each thing goes; each screen decides what goes inside.</bold>
SLOTS.P_3: This way, we don't need a different card for each case: there is <bold>only one card</bold>, and the things that change go in the slots. If a screen doesn't need one of the spaces, we can hide it.
SLOTS.P_4: <bold>For developers, slots make the work much easier.</bold> They are a web standard, so they work in any browser and with any technology. Developers only need to put the real content (the photo, the price, the button) in each space, without changing the component or making new copies. The component takes care of the design, so the result always follows the design of each brand.

TOKENS.TITLE: Variables: one component for 24 brands
TOKENS.FIGMA: In Figma, the variables are organized in <bold>three layers</bold>:
TOKENS.LAYER_1: <bold>Primitive variables</bold> keep the pure values (the color palette).
TOKENS.LAYER_2: <bold>Semantic variables</bold> say what each color is used for (background, text, border, error…).
TOKENS.LAYER_3: <bold>Component variables</bold> say the color of each part of a component (for example, the background of the main button).
TOKENS.LAYERS_LINK: Each layer points to the layer before it.
TOKENS.MODES: The color collections have <bold>only one mode</bold>: desktop and mobile share the same colors, so we don't need to duplicate each color variable for each device. Only <bold>typography, spacing and borders have two modes, desktop and mobile</bold>, because sizes do change depending on the screen.
TOKENS.BRANDS: <bold>Each brand is an extended collection</bold> that inherits everything and only changes what is different (colors, corner radius, fonts…).
TOKENS.REPO: <bold>Tokens come from Figma too.</bold> In our repository, a script reads the Figma variables and creates <bold>one single token file</bold>, with one block for each brand. To change the brand, you only change the data-brand attribute of the page. If you change the value of a token, <bold>all the components that use it change too</bold>.

IN_ACTION.TITLE: The system in action
IN_ACTION.DESCRIPTION: This is how the system works in Figma, with two real components.
IN_ACTION.HEADER_DESC: We start from a <bold>brand-agnostic header</bold>: a component with no brand of its own. With a few clicks, applying the variables of each brand, it becomes three headers with different brands, like our own B travel. It also works the other way: <bold>any of the headers can be adapted to any brand</bold>.
IN_ACTION.CARD_DESC: The card is also brand-agnostic and is built with <bold>slots</bold>, so each brand can add different content. When we apply the brand variables, the visual style changes and <bold>the buttons update automatically</bold>. With one click, we can also <bold>switch the orientation</bold> between horizontal and vertical. And like the headers, every card can be used for any brand, whatever its content.

STEP_TWO.TITLE: Step 2. Today: from Figma to code with AI
STEP_TWO.DESCRIPTION: Without waiting for access to the front-end repository, <bold>AI now builds each component as a Web Component</bold> in our own design repository, following our rules and checking it against Figma.

BUILD.SETUP_1: <bold>We connected AI to Figma.</bold> We used Claude Code with a Figma connector. With the connector, the AI can open our Figma files: it can read the components, the variants, the variables and the sizes, and it can also write in Figma, for example to add a new variant. <bold>The AI can only use our 8 Design System files.</bold> It can't touch anything else.
BUILD.SETUP_2: <bold>We started with a test.</bold> Before working with the real Design System, we tested everything in a separate Figma file, with fake components. We checked that we could go from Figma to code and from code back to Figma, and how a component changes brand. When the test worked, we moved to the real files.
BUILD.SKILLS: <bold>We turned the process into skills</bold>, written recipes that the AI follows step by step. Besides going from Figma to code and back, the AI can <bold>check which components a new design affects</bold> and <bold>what changed in Figma</bold>. This way, anyone in the team can ask in simple words, like <bold>"Turn this Figma component into code"</bold>, and the AI follows the right process.
BUILD.RULES: We didn't write all the rules at the start: <bold>every time something went wrong, we wrote a new rule</bold>, so it doesn't happen again. Today the AI reads them before any work, every change is checked, and <bold>people always have the last word</bold>.
BUILD.SCALE: <bold>We built everything, step by step.</bold> We started with CORE, then icons, logos, B2B and B2C. For big tasks, like almost 400 icons, the AI shared the work between <bold>several agents working at the same time</bold>, and one final review checked everything.
BUILD.MEMORY: <bold>The project has a memory.</bold> Everything is written down, so the work doesn't depend on one person or one conversation:
BUILD.MEM_1: A <bold>status document</bold> says where we are and what comes next.
BUILD.MEM_2: A <bold>learning note</bold> for each component saves what we decided and what to avoid.
BUILD.MEM_3: A <bold>map</bold> connects each Figma component with its code.
BUILD.MEM_4: A <bold>local website</bold> shows every component with all its states.
BUILD.HISTORY: <bold>Every change is recorded</bold> in two places:
BUILD.HIST_1: <bold>In Figma</bold>, in the component description. A designer can see the last change without leaving Figma.
BUILD.HIST_2: <bold>In a shared change history</bold>, with the date, what changed, why, and before and after images.
BUILD.TEAM: <bold>The whole team can use it.</bold> We made a small setup file and a simple guide, so any designer can start in a few minutes. You don't need to know how to code: you just talk to the AI.

ROUND_TRIP.DESCRIPTION: AI connects Figma and code <bold>in both directions</bold>, so design and code stay in sync.

STEP_THREE.TITLE: Step 3. Where we are going: connecting to the real code
STEP_THREE.DESCRIPTION: Everything we build today is ready for that step: <bold>the same names as in Figma, only tokens, written rules and a map between Figma and code.</bold> Connecting it to the real repository will only change where the work goes. We won't need to start from zero.

RESULTS.TITLE: Results
RESULTS.R_1: <bold>CORE complete:</bold> 107 component sets and <bold>1,028 variants</bold>, 100% covered.
RESULTS.R_2: <bold>The 7 component files</bold> (CORE, Icons, Logos, B2B and B2C common and specific) are finished for the scope we defined.
RESULTS.R_3: <bold>More than 500 Web Components</bold> built and checked in our design repository.
RESULTS.R_4: <bold>About 400 icons</bold>, and the components for logos, certifications and payment methods in code.
RESULTS.R_5: <bold>More than 450 learning notes</bold>, one for each component: the knowledge is written down and doesn't depend on one person.
RESULTS.R_6: The same component works for <bold>24 brands</bold> by changing only the tokens.

LEARNINGS.TITLE: What we learned
LEARNINGS.L_1: <bold>AI is as good as the rules you give it.</bold> The most valuable part was not creating code. It was writing our decisions in a way that a person and an AI understand in the same way.
LEARNINGS.L_4: <bold>Documenting is designing.</bold> A system for 24 brands can only grow if anyone can understand why it is made this way.
